questions.text: वनार के सिद्धान्त के अनुसार, केन्द्रीय धातु परमाणु की प्राथमिक संयोजकताएँ:
questions.text_english: According to Werner's theory, the primary valencies of the central metal atom:

options.A: उदासीन अणुओं अथवा ऋणात्मक आयनों द्वारा संतुष्ट होती हैं।
options.B: उपसहसंयोजन संख्या के बराबर होती हैं।
options.C: ऋणात्मक आयनों से संतुष्ट होती हैं।

options_english.A: are satisfied by neutral molecules or negative ions.
options_english.B: are equal to its coordination number.

questions.solution: According to Werner's theory, the primary valencies of the central metal atom are satisfied by negative ions (anions) only. These primary valencies correspond to the oxidation state of the metal and are always ionisable. Option A is incorrect because neutral molecules satisfy secondary valencies (coordination number), not primary ones. Option B confuses primary valencies with coordination number. Option D is wrong because primary valencies are always ionisable; it is the secondary valencies that are non-ionisable.
questions.solution_hindi: वर्नर के सिद्धान्त के अनुसार, केन्द्रीय धातु परमाणु की प्राथमिक संयोजकताएँ केवल ऋणात्मक आयनों द्वारा संतुष्ट होती हैं। ये प्राथमिक संयोजकताएँ धातु की ऑक्सीकरण अवस्था के संगत होती हैं और सदैव आयननीय होती हैं।

questions.text: [Pt(en)2Cl2]2+ में Pt की ऑक्सीकरण संख्या है:
questions.text_english: The oxidation number of Pt in [Pt(en)2Cl2]2+ is:
questions.solution: In [Pt(en)2Cl2]2+, 'en' (ethylenediamine) is a neutral ligand contributing 0 to the charge, and each Cl− contributes −1. The overall charge of the complex ion is +2. Let the oxidation number of Pt be x. Then: x + 2(0) + 2(−1) = +2, which gives x − 2 = +2, so x = +4. Therefore the oxidation number of Pt is +4. Options A, C, and D do not satisfy this charge balance.
questions.solution_hindi: [Pt(en)2Cl2]2+ में 'en' उदासीन लिगैंड है (आवेश = 0) और प्रत्येक Cl− का आवेश −1 है। संकुल का कुल आवेश +2 है। यदि Pt की ऑक्सीकरण संख्या x हो: x + 0 + 0 + (−1) + (−1) = +2 ⟹ x = +4।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा उत्पाद बनता है जब सैलिसिलिक अम्ल को अम्ल की उपस्थिति में (CH3CO)2O के साथ अभिक्रिया किया जाता है?
questions.text_english: Which of the following product is formed when salicylic acid is treated with (CH3CO)2O in the presence of acid?

options.A: Benzene ring with COOCH3 and OH groups (methyl ester of salicylic acid)
options.B: Benzene ring with OCOCH3 and OH groups (aspirin-like with free COOH replaced)
options.C: Benzene ring with COCH3 and COOH groups
options.D: Benzene ring with OCOCH3 and COOH groups (Aspirin)

options_english.A: Benzene ring with COOCH3 and OH (esterification at COOH)
options_english.B: Benzene ring with OCOCH3 and OH (acetylation at OH, COOH replaced)
options_english.C: Benzene ring with COCH3 and COOH
options_english.D: Benzene ring with OCOCH3 and COOH (Aspirin — acetylation at phenolic OH)

questions.solution: When salicylic acid (which has a phenolic −OH and a −COOH group on a benzene ring) reacts with acetic anhydride (CH3CO)2O in the presence of an acid catalyst, the phenolic −OH group undergoes acetylation to give −OCOCH3, while the −COOH group remains intact. The product is 2-acetoxybenzoic acid, commonly known as aspirin, which has the structure shown in option D (OCOCH3 and COOH on the benzene ring). Options A and B are incorrect as they involve esterification of the carboxyl group, and option C is incorrect as it shows acetylation at the ring carbon rather than the oxygen.
questions.solution_hindi: सैलिसिलिक अम्ल में फेनॉलिक −OH और −COOH समूह होते हैं। अम्ल उत्प्रेरक की उपस्थिति में (CH3CO)2O के साथ अभिक्रिया पर फेनॉलिक −OH का एसिटिलीकरण होकर −OCOCH3 बनता है, जबकि −COOH अपरिवर्तित रहता है। उत्पाद ऐस्पिरिन (2-एसिटॉक्सीबेंज़ोइक अम्ल) है — विकल्प D।

questions.text: प्राथमिक, द्वितीयक और तृतीयक ऐमीनों के मध्य विभेद करने के लिए कौन-सा अभिकर्मक प्रयुक्त होता है?
questions.text_english: Which reagent is used to distinguish between primary, secondary and tertiary amines?
questions.solution: Benzenesulphonyl chloride (C6H5SO2Cl), known as Hinsberg's reagent, is used to distinguish between primary, secondary and tertiary amines. Primary amines react with it to give a sulphonamide that is soluble in KOH; secondary amines give a sulphonamide insoluble in KOH; and tertiary amines do not react at all. Option B (benzoyl chloride) can acylate but does not distinguish all three types effectively. Option C (CHCl3 + ethanolic KOH) is the carbylamine test for primary amines only. Option D (NaOH + I2) is the iodoform test for methyl ketones/methyl carbinols.
questions.solution_hindi: बेंजीनसल्फोनिल क्लोराइड (C6H5SO2Cl), जिसे हिन्सबर्ग अभिकर्मक कहते हैं, प्राथमिक, द्वितीयक और तृतीयक ऐमीनों में विभेद करता है। प्राथमिक ऐमीन KOH में विलेय सल्फोनेमाइड देता है; द्वितीयक ऐमीन KOH में अविलेय सल्फोनेमाइड देता है; तृतीयक ऐमीन अभिक्रिया नहीं करता।

questions.text: प्लैटिनम इलेक्ट्रोडों के साथ NaCl के अति तनु जलीय विलयन का विद्युत-अपघटन करने पर:
questions.text_english: On electrolysis of very dilute aqueous solution of NaCl using platinum electrodes:

options.A: ऐनोड पर H2 गैस उत्सर्जित होती है।
options.B: कैथोड पर Na उत्पादित होता है।
options.C: ऐनोड पर O2 गैस उत्सर्जित होती है।
options.D: कैथोड पर H2 गैस उत्सर्जित होती है।

options_english.A: H2 gas is evolved at anode.
options_english.C: O2 gas is evolved at anode.
options_english.D: H2 gas is evolved at cathode.

questions.solution: When a very dilute aqueous solution of NaCl is electrolysed using platinum electrodes, water is preferentially discharged rather than the ions due to the very low concentration of NaCl. At the anode, water is oxidised to release O2 gas: 2H2O → O2 + 4H+ + 4e−. At the cathode, H2O is reduced to produce H2 gas: 2H2O + 2e− → H2 + 2OH−. Option A is incorrect because H2 is released at the cathode, not the anode. Option B is wrong as Na+ ions are not discharged in aqueous solution. Option D is correct for the cathode but the question asks what happens overall, and option C specifically and correctly identifies the anode product.
questions.solution_hindi: अति तनु NaCl विलयन के विद्युत-अपघटन में जल प्राथमिकता से विसर्जित होता है। ऐनोड पर जल का ऑक्सीकरण होकर O2 निकलती है और कैथोड पर H2 निकलती है। Na+ आयन जलीय विलयन में विसर्जित नहीं होता।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित के जलीय विलयन में घटते क्षारकीय प्राबल्य का सही क्रम है:
questions.text_english: The correct order of decreasing basic strength in aqueous solution of the following is:
questions.solution: In aqueous solution, the basic strength of aliphatic amines depends on both the inductive effect of ethyl groups and the solvation (hydration) of the resulting ammonium ions. Diethylamine (C2H5)2NH is the strongest base because it has two electron-donating ethyl groups providing good inductive effect, and the secondary ammonium ion is well solvated. Ethylamine C2H5NH2 comes next as it has one ethyl group and a primary ammonium ion that is effectively solvated. Triethylamine (C2H5)3N is the weakest base in aqueous solution despite having three ethyl groups, because the bulky groups prevent effective solvation of the tertiary ammonium ion. Thus the correct decreasing order is (C2H5)2NH > C2H5NH2 > (C2H5)3N.
questions.solution_hindi: जलीय विलयन में डाइएथिलऐमीन सबसे अधिक क्षारकीय है क्योंकि इंडक्टिव प्रभाव और जलयोजन दोनों अनुकूल हैं। एथिलऐमीन द्वितीय स्थान पर है। ट्राइएथिलऐमीन में तीन एथिल समूह होने के बावजूद स्थूलकाय संरचना के कारण जलयोजन कम होता है, अतः यह सबसे कम क्षारकीय है।
questions.topic: Basic Strength of Amines in Aqueous Solution

questions.text: किसी विलेय के 2·0 मोलल जलीय विलयन में उसका मोल-अंश होता है:
questions.text_english: The mole fraction of a solute in 2·0 molal aqueous solution is:
questions.solution: A 2.0 molal aqueous solution means 2 moles of solute are dissolved in 1 kg (1000 g) of water. Moles of water = 1000/18 = 55.55 mol. Moles of solute = 2 mol. Mole fraction of solute = 2 / (2 + 55.55) = 2 / 57.55 = 0.0347. Therefore the correct answer is option C (0.0347). Option A (1.87) is not a valid mole fraction as it exceeds 1. Option B (0.347) would correspond to a much higher molality. Option D (0.00347) is ten times too small.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित संक्रमण धातुओं में से कौन-सा +1 और +2 ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाएँ दर्शाता है?
questions.text_english: Which of the following transition metals shows +1 and +2 oxidation states?
questions.solution: Copper (Cu) shows both +1 (cuprous) and +2 (cupric) oxidation states. Cu+ (3d10) is formed when Cu loses one electron, and Cu2+ (3d9) is formed when two electrons are lost. Manganese (Mn) shows a wide range from +2 to +7 but not commonly +1. Zinc (Zn) shows only +2. Scandium (Sc) shows only +3 as the stable state. Therefore copper is the correct answer.
questions.solution_hindi: कॉपर (Cu) +1 (क्यूप्रस) और +2 (क्यूप्रिक) दोनों ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाएँ दर्शाता है। Mn +2 से +7 तक दर्शाता है, Zn केवल +2, Sc केवल +3 दर्शाता है।

questions.text: जल-अपघटन करने पर, निम्नलिखित कार्बोहाइड्रेटों में से कौन-सा केवल α-ग्लूकोस देता है?
questions.text_english: On hydrolysis, which of the following carbohydrates gives only α-glucose?
questions.solution: Starch is a polysaccharide made entirely of α-glucose units linked by α-1,4 and α-1,6 glycosidic bonds. On complete hydrolysis, starch gives only α-glucose. Sucrose on hydrolysis gives glucose and fructose (not only glucose). Maltose on hydrolysis gives two molecules of glucose but in the β configuration as well. Cellulose is made of β-glucose units linked by β-1,4 glycosidic bonds and on hydrolysis gives only β-glucose. Therefore starch is the correct answer.
questions.solution_hindi: स्टार्च केवल α-ग्लूकोस इकाइयों का बहुलक है और इसके जल-अपघटन पर केवल α-ग्लूकोस प्राप्त होता है। सुक्रोस से ग्लूकोस + फ्रक्टोस, सेलुलोस से β-ग्लूकोस मिलता है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित यौगिकों पर विचार कीजिए: क्लोरोबेन्जीन (I), 2,4,6-ट्राइनाइट्रोक्लोरोबेन्जीन (II), 2,4-डाइनाइट्रोक्लोरोबेन्जीन (III), 4-नाइट्रोक्लोरोबेन्जीन (IV). इन यौगिकों का नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रियाओं में बढ़ती हुई सुगमता का सही क्रम है:
questions.text_english: Consider the following compounds: Chlorobenzene (I), 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene (II), 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene (III), 4-nitrochlorobenzene (IV). The correct order of increasing ease of nucleophilic substitution reactions of these compounds is:
questions.solution: Nucleophilic aromatic substitution is facilitated by electron-withdrawing groups (like −NO2) at ortho and para positions relative to the leaving group. More −NO2 groups mean greater electron withdrawal from the ring, making the carbon bearing the Cl more electrophilic and easier for nucleophilic attack. Chlorobenzene (I) has no activating −NO2 groups, so it is least reactive. 4-Nitrochlorobenzene (IV) has one −NO2 group at para, giving moderate reactivity. 2,4-Dinitrochlorobenzene (III) has two −NO2 groups. 2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene (II) has three −NO2 groups and is the most reactive. The correct increasing order is I < IV < III < II.
questions.solution_hindi: नाभिकरागी ऐरोमैटिक प्रतिस्थापन में −NO2 समूह (o/p पर) अभिक्रिया को सरल बनाते हैं। −NO2 समूहों की संख्या बढ़ने पर अभिक्रियाशीलता बढ़ती है। सही क्रम: I < IV < III < II।

questions.text: विभिन्न प्रारंभिक दाबों के लिए NH3 के वियोजन की अर्ध-आयु नीचे दी गई हैं: p (टॉर): 704, 75, 34·5; t1/2 (मिनट): 80, 80, 80. अभिक्रिया की कोटि है:
questions.text_english: The half-life periods of decomposition of NH3 for different initial pressures are given below: p (torr): 704, 75, 34·5; t1/2 (min): 80, 80, 80. The order of the reaction is:
questions.solution: For a zero order reaction, the half-life is given by t1/2 = [A]0 / 2k, which means half-life is directly proportional to the initial concentration (or pressure). However, the data shows that despite very different initial pressures (704, 75, and 34.5 torr), the half-life remains constant at 80 minutes. This is the characteristic of a zero order reaction where t1/2 = [A]0/2k, but actually for zero order t1/2 changes with concentration. Wait — for zero order: t1/2 = [A]0/2k which changes. For first order: t1/2 = 0.693/k = constant. Since t1/2 is constant regardless of pressure, this is a first order reaction. Correction: the answer is first order (B), as constant half-life independent of concentration is the hallmark of a first order reaction.
questions.solution_hindi: जब अर्ध-आयु प्रारंभिक सांद्रता (या दाब) से स्वतंत्र हो, तो अभिक्रिया प्रथम कोटि की होती है। यहाँ विभिन्न दाबों पर t1/2 = 80 मिनट स्थिर है, अतः अभिक्रिया प्रथम कोटि की है।

questions.text: द्रव A का 1 मोल और द्रव B के 2 मोल एक विलयन बनाते हैं जिसका कुल वाष्प दाब 40 टॉर है। शुद्ध A और शुद्ध B के वाष्प दाब क्रमश: 30 टॉर और 45 टॉर हैं। उपर्युक्त विलयन:
questions.text_english: 1 mole of liquid A and 2 moles of liquid B make a solution having a total vapour pressure 40 torr. The vapour pressure of pure A and pure B are 30 torr and 45 torr respectively. The above solution:

options.B: राउल्ट के नियम से ऋणात्मक विचलन दर्शाता है।
options.C: राउल्ट के नियम से धनात्मक विचलन दर्शाता है।

options_english.B: shows negative deviation from Raoult's Law.
options_english.C: shows positive deviation from Raoult's Law.

questions.solution: Mole fractions: xA = 1/(1+2) = 1/3, xB = 2/3. Expected (ideal) vapour pressure by Raoult's law = xA × PA° + xB × PB° = (1/3)(30) + (2/3)(45) = 10 + 30 = 40 torr. The observed vapour pressure is also 40 torr, which exactly equals the ideal value. This means the solution is an ideal solution (option A). However, re-checking: 40 torr observed = 40 torr ideal, so this is an ideal solution. The correct answer is A.
questions.solution_hindi: xA = 1/3, xB = 2/3. आदर्श वाष्प दाब = (1/3)(30) + (2/3)(45) = 10 + 30 = 40 टॉर। प्रेक्षित वाष्प दाब भी 40 टॉर है, अतः यह एक आदर्श विलयन है — विकल्प A सही है।

questions.text: अभिकथन (A): ऐल्कोहॉलों के क्वथनांकों की तुलना में ईथरों के क्वथनांक कम होते हैं। कारण (R): यह ऐल्कोहॉलों में हाइड्रोजन आबंधों की उपस्थिति के कारण होता है।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A): Ethers have lower boiling points than the boiling points of alcohols. Reason (R): This is due to the presence of hydrogen bonding in alcohols.
questions.instruction_line: नीचे दिए गए कोडों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from the codes given below.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. Alcohols can form intermolecular hydrogen bonds through their −OH groups, which require significant energy to break, thus raising their boiling points considerably. Ethers lack an O−H bond and cannot form hydrogen bonds with each other (though they can accept H-bonds), so their intermolecular forces are much weaker (only van der Waals), resulting in much lower boiling points compared to alcohols of similar molecular mass. The Reason directly and correctly explains the Assertion.
questions.solution_hindi: दोनों कथन सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है। ऐल्कोहॉलों में −OH समूह के कारण अंतरा-आणविक हाइड्रोजन आबंध बनते हैं जो तोड़ने के लिए अधिक ऊर्जा आवश्यक है, अतः क्वथनांक अधिक होता है। ईथरों में O−H बंध नहीं होता।

questions.text_english: For a reaction A + B → Products, the rate law is: Rate = k[A][B]^(3/2). Write the overall order of the reaction. Can this reaction be an elementary reaction? Give reason in support of your answer.

key_points: Overall order = 1 + 3/2 = 5/2 (or 2.5)
This reaction cannot be an elementary reaction
Because molecularity must be a whole number and cannot be fractional; for elementary reactions, order equals molecularity

questions.solution: The overall order of the reaction is obtained by adding the exponents of the concentration terms in the rate law: order = 1 + 3/2 = 5/2 = 2.5. This reaction cannot be an elementary reaction. For an elementary reaction, the order must equal the molecularity, and molecularity is always a positive whole number (1, 2, or rarely 3). Since the overall order here is 5/2, which is a fractional value, this cannot be a single-step elementary reaction. It must be a complex (multi-step) reaction whose rate law has been determined experimentally.
questions.solution_hindi: समग्र कोटि = 1 + 3/2 = 5/2 = 2.5. यह प्राथमिक अभिक्रिया नहीं हो सकती क्योंकि आण्विकता सदैव पूर्ण संख्या होती है, भिन्नात्मक नहीं। अतः यह जटिल (बहुपदीय) अभिक्रिया है।

questions.text: व्याख्या कीजिए कि क्यों 1 लीटर जल में 1 मोल KCl मिलाने पर जल का क्वथनांक बढ़ जाता है, जबकि 1 लीटर जल में 1 मोल मेथिल ऐल्कोहॉल मिलाने पर जल का क्वथनांक घट जाता है।
questions.text_english: Explain why, on addition of 1 mol of KCl to 1 litre of water, the boiling point of water increases, while the addition of 1 mol of methyl alcohol to 1 litre of water decreases the boiling point.

key_points: KCl is a non-volatile electrolyte; it dissociates to give 2 moles of ions (K+ and Cl−), causing elevation in boiling point (colligative property)
Methyl alcohol is a volatile solute; its addition increases total vapour pressure of the solution above that of pure water, lowering the boiling point

questions.solution: When KCl is added to water, it is a non-volatile electrolyte that dissociates completely into K+ and Cl− ions (effectively 2 moles of particles per mole of KCl). This reduces the vapour pressure of water (Raoult's law), and by the colligative property of elevation of boiling point, the boiling point increases. In contrast, methyl alcohol is a volatile liquid with its own significant vapour pressure. When it is mixed with water, both components contribute to the total vapour pressure of the solution, making the total vapour pressure higher than that of pure water at any given temperature. Since the boiling point is the temperature at which vapour pressure equals atmospheric pressure, a higher vapour pressure means the solution boils at a lower temperature than pure water.

questions.text: आयनों के स्वतंत्र अभिगमन का कोहलराउश का नियम बताइए। एक वक्र की सहायता से व्याख्या कीजिए कि दुर्बल विद्युत-अपघट्यों के लिए सांद्रता − मोलर चालकता वक्र के बहिर्वेशन द्वारा Λ°m का मान ज्ञात क्यों नहीं किया जा सकता है, जिस प्रकार प्रबल विद्युत-अपघट्यों के लिए किया जा सकता है।
questions.text_english: State Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions. With the help of a curve, explain why it is not easy to determine Λ°m for weak electrolytes by extrapolating the concentration − molar conductivity curve, as it is for strong electrolytes.

key_points: Kohlrausch's law: molar conductivity at infinite dilution equals sum of limiting molar conductivities of individual ions
For strong electrolytes: Λm vs √c gives a straight line that can be extrapolated to c=0 to get Λ°m
For weak electrolytes: the curve rises steeply at very low concentrations and does not give a straight line — extrapolation is not reliable

questions.solution:
Kohlrausch's Law of Independent Migration of Ions states that at infinite dilution, each ion migrates independently of the other ions, and the molar conductivity at infinite dilution (Λ°m) of an electrolyte is equal to the sum of the limiting molar conductivities of its individual ions: Λ°m = ν+ λ°+ + ν− λ°−, where ν+ and ν− are the number of cations and anions per formula unit.

For strong electrolytes, the plot of Λm against √c gives a straight line (Debye-Hückel-Onsager equation), which can be extrapolated to zero concentration to obtain Λ°m reliably.

For weak electrolytes (e.g., acetic acid), the degree of dissociation is very low at high concentrations and increases sharply as concentration decreases. Therefore, the molar conductivity rises steeply and in a curved, non-linear fashion at very low concentrations, making it impossible to extrapolate the curve to zero concentration with any accuracy. The curve does not approach a well-defined straight line near zero concentration, so Λ°m cannot be reliably determined by extrapolation for weak electrolytes.

questions.text_english: An antifreeze solution is prepared by dissolving 31 g of ethylene glycol (Molar mass = 62 g mol−1) in 600 g of water. Calculate the freezing point of the solution. (Kf for water = 1·86 K kg mol−1)

key_points: Moles of ethylene glycol = 31/62 = 0.5 mol
Molality = 0.5/0.6 = 0.833 mol/kg
Freezing point = 0 − 1.55 = −1.55°C

questions.solution: Moles of ethylene glycol = 31 g ÷ 62 g mol−1 = 0.5 mol. Mass of solvent (water) = 600 g = 0.6 kg. Molality (m) = moles of solute / mass of solvent in kg = 0.5 / 0.6 = 0.833 mol kg−1. Depression in freezing point: ΔTf = Kf × m = 1.86 × 0.833 = 1.55 K. Freezing point of solution = Freezing point of pure water − ΔTf = 0°C − 1.55°C = −1.55°C. Therefore the freezing point of the antifreeze solution is −1.55°C.

(a) Answer the following questions about the complexes [NiCl4]2− and [Ni(CN)4]2−: (i) Write the hybridization involved in each case. (ii) Which of them is the inner orbital complex and which one is the outer orbital complex? (iii) Compare their magnetic behaviour. [Atomic number: Ni = 28]

sub_questions.text: प्रत्येक प्रकरण में सम्मिलित संकरण लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write the hybridization involved in each case.

key_points: [NiCl4]2−: sp3 hybridization; [Ni(CN)4]2−: dsp2 hybridization

sub_questions.solution: Ni has atomic number 28, ground state configuration [Ar] 3d8 4s2. In complexes, Ni2+ has configuration 3d8. For [NiCl4]2−: Cl− is a weak field ligand, so pairing does not occur in 3d. Ni2+ (3d8) remains with two unpaired electrons and uses sp3 hybridisation (using 4s and three 4p orbitals), forming a tetrahedral geometry. For [Ni(CN)4]2−: CN− is a strong field ligand causing pairing of 3d electrons. One 3d orbital becomes empty, and Ni2+ uses dsp2 hybridisation (one 3d, one 4s, two 4p orbitals), forming a square planar geometry.

sub_questions.text: कौन-सा आंतरिक कक्षक संकुल है और कौन-सा बाह्य कक्षक संकुल है?
sub_questions.text_english: Which is the inner orbital complex and which is the outer orbital complex?

key_points: [Ni(CN)4]2− is the inner orbital complex (dsp2); [NiCl4]2− is the outer orbital complex (sp3)

sub_questions.solution: [Ni(CN)4]2− is the inner orbital complex because its hybridisation is dsp2, involving a 3d orbital (inner d orbital) from the penultimate shell. [NiCl4]2− is the outer orbital complex because it uses sp3 hybridisation involving only 4s and 4p orbitals (outer orbitals), without using any 3d orbital from the penultimate shell.

sub_questions.text: इनके चुम्बकीय व्यवहार की तुलना कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Compare their magnetic behaviour.

key_points: [NiCl4]2− is paramagnetic (2 unpaired electrons); [Ni(CN)4]2− is diamagnetic (0 unpaired electrons)

sub_questions.solution: [NiCl4]2− has sp3 hybridisation with Ni2+ retaining its 3d8 configuration with two unpaired electrons. Therefore it is paramagnetic. [Ni(CN)4]2− has dsp2 hybridisation: CN− forces pairing of all 3d electrons so Ni2+ has the configuration 3d8 with all electrons paired. Therefore it is diamagnetic.

sub_questions.text_english: Name two coordination compounds which are important in biological systems.

key_points: Haemoglobin (iron porphyrin complex) and Chlorophyll (magnesium porphyrin complex)

sub_questions.solution: Two important coordination compounds in biological systems are: (1) Haemoglobin — a complex of iron(II) with a porphyrin ring (haem group) and protein (globin); it carries oxygen in blood. (2) Chlorophyll — a complex of magnesium with a porphyrin ring present in green plants; it is responsible for photosynthesis.

sub_questions.text: कीलेट प्रभाव से क्या अभिप्राय है? एक उदाहरण दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: What is meant by chelate effect? Give an example.

key_points: Chelate effect: chelate complexes (formed by polydentate ligands) are more stable than similar complexes with unidentate ligands; example: [Ni(en)3]2+ is more stable than [Ni(NH3)6]2+

sub_questions.solution: The chelate effect refers to the enhanced stability of a complex formed by a polydentate (chelating) ligand compared to a complex formed by an equivalent number of monodentate ligands. This extra stability arises because chelate ring formation increases entropy (more particles released when monodentate ligands are displaced). For example, [Ni(en)3]2+ (formed by three bidentate ethylenediamine ligands) is significantly more stable than [Ni(NH3)6]2+ (formed by six monodentate ammonia ligands).

sub_questions.text: निम्न प्रचक्रण चतुष्फलकीय संकुल विरले ही क्यों बनते हैं?
sub_questions.text_english: Why are low spin tetrahedral complexes rarely formed?

key_points: Crystal field splitting in tetrahedral complexes (Δt) is much smaller (about 4/9 of Δo), so pairing energy always exceeds Δt, making low spin configuration energetically unfavourable

sub_questions.solution: Low spin tetrahedral complexes are rarely formed because the crystal field splitting energy in tetrahedral complexes (Δt) is only about 4/9 of the octahedral splitting energy (Δo) for the same ligand and metal. This smaller value of Δt is almost always less than the electron pairing energy. Since pairing electrons requires more energy than simply filling the higher energy d orbitals, electrons prefer to remain unpaired, resulting in high spin configurations. Therefore, even with strong field ligands, the splitting is too small to force electron pairing in a tetrahedral geometry, and low spin tetrahedral complexes are very rare.

sub_questions.text: ऐनिलीन से सल्फैनिलिक अम्ल
sub_questions.text_english: Sulphanilic acid from aniline

key_points: Aniline + conc. H2SO4 → anilinium hydrogen sulphate → heat (baking) → sulphanilic acid (4-aminobenzenesulphonic acid)

sub_questions.solution: Aniline is treated with concentrated sulphuric acid to form anilinium hydrogen sulphate (C6H5NH3+HSO4−). On heating this salt ('baking'), the sulphonic acid group migrates to the para position giving sulphanilic acid (4-aminobenzenesulphonic acid): C6H5NH2 + H2SO4 → C6H5NH3+ HSO4− → heat → 4-H2N-C6H4-SO3H (sulphanilic acid).

key_points: Aniline + excess Br2 water → 2,4,6-tribromoaniline (white precipitate) + 3HBr

sub_questions.solution: When aniline is treated with excess bromine water (Br2/H2O) at room temperature, the −NH2 group strongly activates the benzene ring towards electrophilic substitution. Bromine simultaneously substitutes at the 2, 4, and 6 positions (ortho and para) to give 2,4,6-tribromoaniline as a white precipitate: C6H5NH2 + 3Br2 → 2,4,6-Br3C6H2NH2 + 3HBr.

key_points: Aniline + acetic anhydride (CH3CO)2O → acetanilide + acetic acid (acetylation)

sub_questions.solution: Aniline undergoes acetylation when treated with acetic anhydride (or acetyl chloride) in the presence of a base (pyridine or glacial acetic acid). The −NH2 group reacts with (CH3CO)2O to give acetanilide (N-phenylethanamide): C6H5NH2 + (CH3CO)2O → C6H5NHCOCH3 (acetanilide) + CH3COOH.

questions.text: C3H5N आण्विक सूत्र का एक कार्बनिक यौगिक (A), C6H5MgBr के साथ अभिक्रिया करने के उपरान्त जल-अपघटन करने पर यौगिक (B) देता है। यौगिक (B), 2,4-डी.एन.पी. अभिकर्मक के साथ नारंगी-लाल अवक्षेप देता है तथा आयोडोफॉर्म परीक्षण नहीं देता है। यह टॉलेन्स अभिकर्मक अथवा फेलिंग अभिकर्मक को अपचित नहीं करता है और न ही ब्रोमीन जल को वर्णविहीन करता है। यह क्रोमिक अम्ल द्वारा प्रबल ऑक्सीकरण से एक कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्ल (C) बनाता है जिसका आण्विक सूत्र C7H6O2 है। यौगिक (A), (B) और (C) को पहचानिए। यौगिक (A) की C6H5MgBr के साथ अभिक्रिया करने के उपरान्त जल-अपघटन करने पर यौगिक (B) बनने की अभिक्रियाएँ लिखिए।
questions.text_english: An organic compound (A) with molecular formula C3H5N on reaction with C6H5MgBr followed by hydrolysis, gives a compound (B). Compound (B) forms an orange-red precipitate with 2,4-DNP reagent and does not give iodoform test. It neither reduces Tollens' or Fehling's reagent nor does it decolourise bromine water. On drastic oxidation with chromic acid it gives a carboxylic acid (C) having molecular formula C7H6O2. Identify the compounds (A), (B) and (C). Write the reactions of compound (A) with C6H5MgBr followed by hydrolysis to give compound (B).

key_points: A = CH3CN (ethanenitrile / acetonitrile, C2H3N — actually C3H5N: acrylonitrile CH2=CHCN or propionitrile C2H5CN); most consistent: A = CH3CH2CN (propionitrile)
B = C6H5COC2H5 (phenyl ethyl ketone / propiophenone) — 2,4-DNP positive, no iodoform (no CH3CO), no Tollens, no Fehling
C = C6H5COOH (benzoic acid, C7H6O2)

questions.solution:
Compound (A) is propionitrile (CH3CH2CN, C3H5N). When (A) reacts with phenyl magnesium bromide (C6H5MgBr, a Grignard reagent) followed by hydrolysis, the nitrile group reacts with C6H5MgBr to first form an imine salt intermediate, which on hydrolysis gives compound (B): phenyl ethyl ketone (propiophenone, C6H5COC2H5).

Compound (B) gives an orange-red precipitate with 2,4-DNP (confirms carbonyl group — ketone), does not give iodoform test (no CH3CO− group), does not reduce Tollens' or Fehling's reagent (confirms it is a ketone, not an aldehyde), and does not decolourise bromine water (no C=C double bond).

On drastic oxidation with chromic acid, the C6H5CO− part is oxidised to benzoic acid (C6H5COOH), molecular formula C7H6O2, which is compound (C).

Reactions: CH3CH2CN + C6H5MgBr → CH3CH2C(=NMgBr)C6H5 (addition product) → H3O+/H2O → CH3CH2CO-C6H5 (propiophenone, B) + NH3.
questions.solution_hindi: (A) = प्रोपेनाइट्राइल (CH3CH2CN); (B) = फेनिल एथिल कीटोन (C6H5COC2H5, प्रोपियोफेनोन); (C) = बेन्जोइक अम्ल (C6H5COOH)। ग्रीन्यार अभिकर्मक नाइट्राइल से जोड़कर, जल-अपघटन पर कीटोन देता है।

questions.text: किसी रेडियोसक्रिय तत्त्व की अर्ध-आयु 1·5 × 10^10 वर्ष है। उस समय का परिकलन कीजिए जिसमें तत्त्व की सक्रियता उसके प्रारंभिक मान से घटकर 75% रह जाती है। [दिया गया है: log 2 = 0·30, log 3 = 0·48, log 4 = 0·60]
questions.text_english: The half-life period of a radioactive element is 1·5 × 10^10 years. Calculate the time in which the activity of the element is reduced to 75% of its original value. [Given: log 2 = 0·30, log 3 = 0·48, log 4 = 0·60]

key_points: Activity reduced to 75% means N/N0 = 0.75 = 3/4

questions.solution:
The activity of a radioactive element is directly proportional to the number of atoms N. Activity reduced to 75% means N = 0.75 N0 = (3/4)N0.

Decay constant λ = 0.693 / t1/2 = 0.693 / (1.5 × 10^10) yr−1.

Using the first order decay equation: t = (2.303/λ) × log(N0/N) = (2.303 × t1/2 / 0.693) × log(N0/N)

t = (2.303 × 1.5 × 10^10 / 0.693) × log(4/3)
= (2.303 × 1.5 × 10^10 / 0.693) × (log 4 − log 3)
= (2.303 × 1.5 × 10^10 / 0.693) × (0.60 − 0.48)
= (2.303 × 1.5 × 10^10 / 0.693) × 0.12
= (3.4545 × 10^10 / 0.693) × 0.12
= 4.986 × 10^10 × 0.12
= 0.623 × 10^10
≈ 6.23 × 10^9 years.

Therefore the time required for the activity to reduce to 75% of its original value is approximately 6.23 × 10^9 years.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित के लिए कारण दीजिए: (क) हैलोऐल्केनें KCN के साथ अभिक्रिया करके ऐल्किल सायनाइड बनाते हैं, जबकि AgCN के साथ यह आइसोसायनाइड बनाते हैं। (ख) SN2 प्रतिस्थापन के प्रति साइक्लोहेक्सिलमेथिल क्लोराइड, साइक्लोहेक्सिल क्लोराइड की तुलना में अधिक अभिक्रियाशील है। (ग) ग्रीन्यार अभिकर्मक का विरचन निर्जलीय अवस्थाओं में करना चाहिए।
questions.text_english: Give reasons for the following: (a) Haloalkanes react with KCN to form alkyl cyanides, while with AgCN, they form isocyanides. (b) Cyclohexylmethyl chloride (−CH2Cl) is more reactive towards SN2 displacement as compared to cyclohexyl chloride (−Cl). (c) Grignard reagents should be prepared under anhydrous conditions.

sub_questions.text: हैलोऐल्केनें KCN के साथ ऐल्किल सायनाइड और AgCN के साथ आइसोसायनाइड क्यों बनाते हैं?
sub_questions.text_english: Haloalkanes react with KCN to form alkyl cyanides, while with AgCN they form isocyanides. Give reason.

key_points: KCN is ionic; CN− attacks through C (soft nucleophile) to give R−CN. AgCN is covalent; Ag bonds to N, so C is free to attack giving R−NC (isocyanide)

sub_questions.solution: KCN is predominantly ionic in nature. The cyanide ion (CN−) is an ambidentate nucleophile that can attack through either C or N. In KCN, the carbon end of CN− acts as the nucleophile (being a softer base and more polarisable), attacking the carbon of the haloalkane to give alkyl cyanide (R−CN). In AgCN, the salt is covalent; silver is bonded to nitrogen, leaving the carbon end free. Therefore, the carbon of the haloalkane attacks through the nitrogen end, giving an isocyanide (R−NC).

sub_questions.text: SN2 प्रतिस्थापन के प्रति साइक्लोहेक्सिलमेथिल क्लोराइड अधिक अभिक्रियाशील क्यों है?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is cyclohexylmethyl chloride more reactive towards SN2 than cyclohexyl chloride?

key_points: In cyclohexyl chloride, the C−Cl carbon is in the ring and secondary, causing steric hindrance to rear attack. In cyclohexylmethyl chloride, the C−Cl carbon is exocyclic and primary — less hindered, easier for SN2 back-attack.

sub_questions.solution: In SN2 reactions, the nucleophile attacks the carbon bearing the leaving group from the back (backside attack). In cyclohexyl chloride, the C−Cl bond is directly on the ring (secondary carbon), and the two flanking ring carbons cause significant steric hindrance to the approaching nucleophile, slowing SN2. In cyclohexylmethyl chloride (−CH2Cl), the chlorine is on a primary carbon that is exocyclic (outside the ring). This primary carbon has much less steric crowding, allowing the nucleophile to approach more easily, making SN2 faster.

sub_questions.text: ग्रीन्यार अभिकर्मक का विरचन निर्जलीय अवस्थाओं में क्यों करना चाहिए?
sub_questions.text_english: Why should Grignard reagents be prepared under anhydrous conditions?

key_points: Grignard reagents (RMgX) are highly reactive towards water/protic solvents — they react with any H bonded to O or N to give a hydrocarbon, destroying the reagent

sub_questions.solution: Grignard reagents (R−MgX) are extremely reactive because the C−Mg bond is highly polarised, with carbon carrying a partial negative charge (carbanion-like). Any traces of moisture (H2O) or protic substances react immediately with the Grignard reagent to protonate the carbanion, producing a hydrocarbon and destroying the reagent: R−MgX + H2O → R−H + Mg(OH)X. Therefore, strict anhydrous conditions (dry ether, dry glassware) are essential during preparation and use of Grignard reagents.

questions.text: जैव-तंत्र अनेक जटिल जैव अणुओं जैसे कार्बोहाइड्रेट, प्रोटीन, न्यूक्लिक अम्ल, लिपिड, आदि से मिलकर बनते हैं। प्रोटीन और कार्बोहाइड्रेट हमारे भोजन के आवश्यक अवयव हैं। इसके अतिरिक्त कुछ सरल अणु जैसे विटामिन और खनिज लवण भी जीवों की कार्य-प्रणालियों में महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाते हैं। सभी प्रोटीन α-ऐमीनो अम्लों के बहुलक होते हैं। आण्विक आकृति के आधार पर प्रोटीनों को दो वर्गों में वर्गीकृत किया जा सकता है — रेशेदार प्रोटीन और गोलिकाकार प्रोटीन। विटामिन आहार में आवश्यक सहायक भोज्य कारक हैं। इन्हें वसा-विलेय तथा जल-विलेय में वर्गीकृत किया जाता है। विटामिनों की कमी से अनेक रोग हो जाते हैं। न्यूक्लिक अम्ल न्यूक्लिओटाइडों के बहुलक हैं जो एक क्षारक, एक पेन्टोस शर्करा तथा एक फॉस्फेट अवशांश से मिलकर बनते हैं। न्यूक्लिक अम्ल दो प्रकार के होते हैं — DNA और RNA। न्यूक्लिक अम्ल जनक से संतति में गुणों के स्थानांतरण के लिए जिम्मेदार होते हैं।
questions.text_english: Living systems are made up of various complex biomolecules like carbohydrates, proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, etc. Proteins and carbohydrates are essential constituents of our food. In addition, some simple molecules like vitamins and mineral salts also play an important role in the functions of organisms. All proteins are polymers of α-amino acids. Proteins can be classified into two types on the basis of their molecular shape — Fibrous and Globular proteins. Vitamins are accessory food factors required in the diet. They are classified as fat-soluble and water-soluble. Deficiency of vitamins leads to many diseases. Nucleic acids are the polymers of nucleotides which in turn consist of a base, a pentose sugar and phosphate moiety. There are two types of nucleic acids — DNA and RNA. Nucleic acids are responsible for the transfer of characters from parents to offsprings.

questions.instruction_line_english: Read the case carefully and answer the questions that follow.

sub_questions.text: प्रोटीनों और न्यूक्लिक अम्लों की मूल संरचनात्मक इकाइयों के नाम लिखिए। आप रेशेदार और गोलिकाकार प्रोटीन में उनकी संरचनाओं के आधार पर कैसे अंतर कर सकते हो?
sub_questions.text_english: Write the name of basic building units of proteins and nucleic acids. How can you differentiate between Fibrous and Globular proteins on the basis of their structures?

key_points: Basic unit of proteins: α-amino acids; basic unit of nucleic acids: nucleotides
Fibrous proteins: polypeptide chains run parallel, held by H-bonds, giving fibre-like structure; insoluble in water; e.g., keratin, collagen
Globular proteins: polypeptide chains coil into spherical shape; generally soluble in water; e.g., insulin, albumin

sub_questions.solution: The basic building unit of proteins is the α-amino acid. The basic building unit of nucleic acids is the nucleotide (consisting of a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar, and a phosphate group). Fibrous proteins have polypeptide chains arranged parallel or coiled along a single axis, held together by hydrogen bonds and disulphide bonds, giving a thread-like or fibrous structure; they are insoluble in water and serve structural roles (e.g., keratin in hair, collagen in connective tissue). Globular proteins have polypeptide chains folded and coiled back upon themselves to give a compact, spherical shape; they are generally soluble in water and perform physiological functions such as enzyme catalysis and hormone action (e.g., insulin, haemoglobin).

sub_questions.text: जब DNA के थायमीन युक्त न्यूक्लिओटाइड का जल-अपघटन किया जाए तो कौन-कौन से उत्पाद बनेंगे?
sub_questions.text_english: What products would be formed when a nucleotide from DNA containing thymine is hydrolyzed?

key_points: Products: Thymine (base) + Deoxyribose (2-deoxyribose, pentose sugar) + Phosphoric acid (H3PO4)

sub_questions.solution: When a nucleotide from DNA containing thymine is hydrolysed, three components are obtained: (1) Thymine — the nitrogenous base (a pyrimidine); (2) 2-Deoxyribose — the pentose sugar present in DNA (deoxyribose lacks the −OH at C-2); and (3) Phosphoric acid (H3PO4) — the phosphate moiety.

questions.text_english: Alcohols have higher boiling points than other compounds, namely hydrocarbons, ethers and haloalkanes of comparable molecular masses. On oxidation, primary alcohols yield aldehydes with mild oxidizing agents and carboxylic acids with strong oxidizing agents. Secondary alcohols yield ketones on oxidation while tertiary alcohols are resistant to oxidation. Ethers may be prepared by dehydration of alcohols and Williamson synthesis. The C−O bond in ethers can be cleaved by hydrogen halides. The presence of −OH group in phenols activates the aromatic ring towards electrophilic substitution and directs the incoming group to ortho and para positions due to resonance effect. In presence of NaOH, phenol generates phenoxide ion which is even more reactive than phenol. Thus, in alkaline medium, phenol undergoes Kolbe's reaction.

key_points: (i) Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) in CH2Cl2, or MnO2
(ii) Acidified KMnO4 or acidified K2Cr2O7

sub_questions.solution: For oxidation of a primary alcohol to an aldehyde, a mild oxidising agent is used: Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC, ClCrO3·C5H5N) in dichloromethane (CH2Cl2) is the most common reagent; MnO2 is also used for allylic/benzylic alcohols. For oxidation of a primary alcohol all the way to a carboxylic acid, a strong oxidising agent is required: acidified potassium permanganate (KMnO4/H2SO4) or acidified potassium dichromate (K2Cr2O7/H2SO4).

sub_questions.text_english: Write the reaction involved in Kolbe's reaction.

key_points: Phenol + NaOH → sodium phenoxide; then CO2 under pressure/heat → sodium salicylate; then H+ → salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid)

sub_questions.solution: In Kolbe's reaction, sodium phenoxide (C6H5ONa) is treated with CO2 under pressure at about 400 K. The carboxylate group is introduced at the ortho position to give sodium salicylate. Subsequent acidification gives salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid): C6H5ONa + CO2 (pressure, 400K) → HOC6H4COONa (sodium salicylate) → H+ → HOC6H4COOH (salicylic acid).

sub_questions.text_english: Why are tertiary alcohols resistant to oxidation?

key_points: Tertiary alcohols have no α-hydrogen atom (the carbon bearing −OH has no H), so oxidation which requires removal of an α-H cannot occur under normal conditions

sub_questions.solution: Tertiary alcohols are resistant to oxidation because the carbon atom bearing the −OH group (the α-carbon) has no hydrogen atom attached to it — it is bonded to three other carbon groups. Oxidation of alcohols requires the removal of a hydrogen from the α-carbon along with the −OH group to form a carbonyl compound. Since no such α-hydrogen is available in a tertiary alcohol, the oxidation does not proceed under mild or moderately strong conditions.

sub_questions.solution: When an unsymmetrical ether containing one tert-alkyl group reacts with HI, the iodide ion (I−, the nucleophile) attacks the less hindered alkyl group, and the more stable tertiary carbocation/or simple SN2 at the primary carbon occurs. sub_questions.text_english: Product when one mol of ethanal is treated with 1 mol of CH3OH in the presence of dry HCl gas.

key_points: CH3CH(OCH3)OH → then loses water → CH3CH(OCH3)2? No — 1 mol methanol: hemiacetal: CH3CH(OH)(OCH3) (acetaldehyde methyl hemiacetal)

sub_questions.solution: When one mole of ethanal (CH3CHO) is treated with one mole of methanol (CH3OH) in the presence of dry HCl, an addition reaction occurs at the carbonyl group. The methanol adds across the C=O bond to form a hemiacetal: CH3CHO + CH3OH → CH3CH(OH)(OCH3) (1-methoxyethanol, the hemiacetal). With one mole of alcohol only the hemiacetal is formed; an acetal would require two moles of alcohol.

sub_questions.text: बेन्जैल्डिहाइड को सांद्र NaOH के साथ अभिक्रिया — उत्पाद।
sub_questions.text_english: Product when benzaldehyde is treated with conc. NaOH.

key_points: Cannizzaro reaction: one mole of benzaldehyde is oxidised to benzoic acid (C6H5COONa) and one mole is reduced to benzyl alcohol (C6H5CH2OH)

sub_questions.solution: Benzaldehyde has no α-hydrogen, so it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction (disproportionation) when treated with concentrated NaOH. One molecule is oxidised and the other is reduced: 2C6H5CHO + NaOH (conc.) → C6H5COONa (sodium benzoate) + C6H5CH2OH (benzyl alcohol). On acidification, sodium benzoate gives benzoic acid.

key_points: Acetic anhydride (CH3CO)2O is formed by dehydration

sub_questions.solution: When ethanoic acid (acetic acid, CH3COOH) is heated in the presence of P2O5 (a strong dehydrating agent), intermolecular dehydration occurs between two molecules of acetic acid to form acetic anhydride: 2CH3COOH → (CH3CO)2O + H2O.

sub_questions.text_english: A simple chemical test to distinguish between Ethanal and Propanal.

key_points: Iodoform test: ethanal (CH3CHO) gives yellow iodoform precipitate with I2/NaOH; propanal (CH3CH2CHO) does not give iodoform test

sub_questions.solution: The iodoform test can distinguish between ethanal and propanal. When treated with iodine and NaOH (I2/NaOH), ethanal (CH3CHO) gives a yellow precipitate of iodoform (CHI3) because it contains the CH3CO− group. Propanal (CH3CH2CHO) does not give a positive iodoform test since it lacks the CH3CO− group. The appearance of a yellow precipitate with characteristic antiseptic smell identifies ethanal.

sub_questions.text_english: Name of the reagent to transform Allyl alcohol to Propenal.

key_points: MnO2 (manganese dioxide) — a mild oxidising agent for allylic/benzylic alcohols

sub_questions.solution: Allyl alcohol (prop-2-en-1-ol, CH2=CHCH2OH) is converted to propenal (acrolein, CH2=CHCHO) by selective oxidation of the primary allylic alcohol to an aldehyde using manganese dioxide (MnO2) as the reagent. MnO2 is a mild oxidising agent that selectively oxidises allylic and benzylic alcohols to the corresponding carbonyl compounds without affecting the C=C double bond.

sub_questions.text_english: Draw the structure of the semicarbazone of acetone.

key_points: CH3−C(=N−NH−CONH2)−CH3 (acetone semicarbazone)

sub_questions.solution: Acetone (CH3COCH3) reacts with semicarbazide (NH2−NH−CONH2) to form the semicarbazone by condensation. The structure of acetone semicarbazone is: CH3−C(=N−NH−CO−NH2)−CH3. The carbonyl oxygen of acetone is replaced by =N−NH−CONH2 group, forming a C=N bond.

sub_questions.text: ऐल्डिहाइडों और कीटोनों के α-हाइड्रोजन परमाणुओं की प्रकृति अम्लीय क्यों होती है?
sub_questions.text_english: Why are α-hydrogen atoms of aldehydes and ketones acidic in nature?

key_points: The α-carbon is adjacent to the carbonyl group; the C=O withdraws electron density, weakening the C−H bond at α-carbon; the resulting carbanion (enolate) is stabilised by resonance with the carbonyl group

sub_questions.solution: The α-hydrogen atoms in aldehydes and ketones are acidic because the α-carbon is adjacent to the strongly electron-withdrawing carbonyl group (C=O). The inductive and resonance effects of the C=O group weaken the C−H bond at the α-carbon. When the α-hydrogen is removed (by a base) to form a carbanion, the resulting negative charge is stabilised by resonance delocalisation into the carbonyl group, forming a stable enolate ion. This resonance stabilisation of the carbanion makes the removal of the α-hydrogen easier, giving it acidic character.

sub_questions.text: HCN के प्रति अभिक्रियाशीलता के बढ़ते क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए: CH3COCH3, CH3CHO, (CH3)3C−C(=O)−CH3
sub_questions.text_english: Arrange in increasing order of reactivity towards HCN: CH3COCH3, CH3CHO, (CH3)3C−C(=O)−CH3

key_points: Increasing order: (CH3)3C−CO−CH3 < CH3COCH3 < CH3CHO

sub_questions.solution: Reactivity towards HCN (nucleophilic addition) depends on: (1) the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon — electron-withdrawing groups increase reactivity; (2) steric hindrance — bulkier groups around the carbonyl decrease reactivity. Aldehydes are more reactive than ketones due to less steric hindrance and greater positive charge on carbonyl carbon. Among ketones, greater bulkiness decreases reactivity. CH3CHO (ethanal, an aldehyde) is most reactive. CH3COCH3 (acetone) is less reactive than ethanal. (CH3)3C−CO−CH3 (methyl tert-butyl ketone) is least reactive due to the very bulky tert-butyl group. Increasing order of reactivity: (CH3)3C−CO−CH3 < CH3COCH3 < CH3CHO.

sub_questions.text_english: Write the reaction involved in Etard reaction.

key_points: Toluene + chromyl chloride (CrO2Cl2) in CCl4 → chromium complex intermediate → hydrolysis → benzaldehyde

sub_questions.solution: The Etard reaction involves the oxidation of an alkyl side chain of an aromatic compound directly to an aldehyde using chromyl chloride (CrO2Cl2) in CS2 or CCl4 as solvent. The methyl group of toluene is oxidised to give a brown chromium complex which on hydrolysis with water gives benzaldehyde: C6H5−CH3 + 2CrO2Cl2 → C6H5−CH(OCrOHCl2)2 (Etard complex) → H2O → C6H5−CHO (benzaldehyde) + Cr compounds.

sub_questions.text_english: Write the product when cyclohexanecarbaldehyde reacts with Zn(Hg)/conc. HCl.

key_points: Cyclohexanecarbaldehyde (cyclohexyl-CHO) + Zn(Hg)/conc. HCl → methylcyclohexane (Clemmensen reduction: −CHO → −CH3)

sub_questions.solution: Zn(Hg)/conc. HCl is the Clemmensen reduction reagent, which reduces a carbonyl group (C=O) directly to a methylene group (−CH2−) or methyl group. When cyclohexanecarbaldehyde (C6H11−CHO) undergoes Clemmensen reduction, the −CHO group is reduced to −CH3, giving methylcyclohexane (C6H11−CH3).

sub_questions.solution:
Using the Nernst equation for the half-cell Zn2+(aq) + 2e− → Zn(s):
E = E° − (0.0591/n) × log(1/[Zn2+])
E = −0.76 − (0.0591/2) × log(1/0.01)
= −0.76 − (0.02955) × log(100)
= −0.76 − (0.02955) × 2  [since log 100 = 2 × log 10 = 2 × 1 = 2]
= −0.76 − 0.0591
= −0.8191 V
Therefore the electrode potential of the half-cell is −0.8191 V (approximately −0.819 V).

Cathode: MnO2 + NH4+ + e− → MnO(OH) + NH3
Overall: Zn + 2MnO2 + 2NH4+ → Zn2+ + 2MnO(OH) + 2NH3

sub_questions.solution: In a dry cell (Leclanche cell), the electrode reactions are as follows. At the anode (zinc container), oxidation occurs: Zn(s) → Zn2+(aq) + 2e−. At the cathode (carbon rod surrounded by MnO2 and NH4Cl paste), reduction occurs: MnO2(s) + NH4+(aq) + e− → MnO(OH)(s) + NH3(g). The overall cell reaction is: Zn(s) + 2MnO2(s) + 2NH4+(aq) → Zn2+(aq) + 2MnO(OH)(s) + 2NH3(g).

sub_questions.text: साम्य स्थिरांक (Kc), E°सेल से संबंधित है परन्तु Eसेल से नहीं — क्यों?
sub_questions.text_english: Equilibrium constant (Kc) is related to E°cell, but not to Ecell. Why?

key_points: At equilibrium, ΔG° = −nFE°cell = −RT ln Kc; Kc is related to ΔG°, which is related to standard conditions (E°cell). The non-standard Ecell changes with concentration (Nernst equation) and at equilibrium Ecell = 0, not E°cell.

sub_questions.solution: The equilibrium constant Kc is related to the standard Gibbs free energy change: ΔG° = −RT ln Kc. The standard Gibbs energy is also related to the standard electrode potential: ΔG° = −nFE°cell. Therefore Kc is related to E°cell through: ln Kc = nFE°cell/RT. Both ΔG° and E°cell refer to standard conditions (unit activity, 1 M concentrations, 298 K), which is the same standard state used to define Kc. The non-standard cell potential Ecell (given by the Nernst equation) changes with the actual concentrations and is equal to zero when the cell reaches equilibrium. Therefore, Kc cannot be related to Ecell (which varies and becomes zero at equilibrium).

sub_questions.text: मोलर चालकता एवं वियोजन मात्रा (α) परिकलित कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Calculate molar conductivity and degree of dissociation (α) of acetic acid.
sub_questions.solution:
Given: conductivity κ = 3.905 × 10−5 S cm−1, concentration C = 0.001 M = 0.001 mol L−1.

Molar conductivity: Λm = (κ × 1000) / C = (3.905 × 10−5 × 1000) / 0.001 = 3.905 × 10−2 / 10−3 = 39.05 S cm2 mol−1.

Limiting molar conductivity of acetic acid: Λ°m(CH3COOH) = λ°H+ + λ°CH3COO− = 349.6 + 40.9 = 390.5 S cm2 mol−1.

Degree of dissociation: α = Λm / Λ°m = 39.05 / 390.5 = 0.10 (i.e., 10%).

Therefore, the molar conductivity is 39.05 S cm2 mol−1 and the degree of dissociation is 0.10 (10%).

sub_questions.text: मर्क्युरी सेल अपनी संपूर्ण कार्य अवधि में स्थिर वोल्टता क्यों प्रदान करता है?
sub_questions.text_english: Why does a mercury cell deliver a constant voltage for its entire life?

key_points: The overall cell reaction does not involve any ions in solution (HgO is reduced to Hg, Zn is oxidised), so the electrolyte concentration does not change, keeping the cell potential constant throughout its life

sub_questions.solution: A mercury cell delivers constant voltage throughout its life because the cell reaction does not involve any solution-phase ions whose concentration could change during discharge. In the mercury cell, the anode is zinc amalgam (Zn/Hg) and the cathode is a paste of HgO and carbon. The cell reactions are: Anode: Zn(Hg) + 2OH− → ZnO(s) + H2O + 2e−; Cathode: HgO(s) + H2O + 2e− → Hg(l) + 2OH−. Since the OH− ions consumed at the anode are regenerated at the cathode, their concentration remains constant, and hence the cell potential (which depends on ion concentrations via the Nernst equation) remains constant throughout the cell's life.

sub_questions.text: गैल्वैनी सेल में लवण सेतु का उपयोग करना क्यों आवश्यक है?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is it necessary to use salt bridge in a galvanic cell?

key_points: Salt bridge maintains electrical neutrality in both half-cells by allowing migration of ions (cations to cathode half-cell, anions to anode half-cell), thus completing the internal circuit and enabling continuous current flow

sub_questions.solution: A salt bridge is necessary in a galvanic cell for two reasons. First, it maintains electrical neutrality in both half-cells: as the cell operates, the anode solution accumulates positive ions (e.g., Zn2+) and needs anions, while the cathode solution depletes positive ions and needs cations. The salt bridge allows ions from the KCl/KNO3 solution to migrate in both directions to balance the charges. Second, it completes the internal circuit of the cell, allowing ionic current to flow between the two half-cells without mixing the electrode solutions, enabling continuous generation of electrical energy.

sub_questions.text: Fe अथवा Cu — उच्चतर गलनांक कौन-सा और क्यों?
sub_questions.text_english: Fe or Cu — which has higher melting point and why?

key_points: Fe has a higher melting point (1535°C) than Cu (1083°C) because Fe has more unpaired d-electrons available for metallic bonding, leading to stronger metallic bonds

sub_questions.solution: Iron (Fe) has a higher melting point than copper (Cu). Fe has the electronic configuration [Ar] 3d6 4s2, with four unpaired d-electrons contributing to strong metallic bonding. Cu has configuration [Ar] 3d10 4s1 with a completely filled 3d subshell and only the 4s electron available for metallic bonding. More unpaired electrons in Fe result in stronger interatomic metallic bonds, requiring more energy (higher temperature) to break them, giving Fe a higher melting point (1535°C) compared to Cu (1083°C).

sub_questions.text: Ti3+ अथवा Sc3+ — जलीय विलयन में रंगीन कौन-सा और क्यों?
sub_questions.text_english: Ti3+ or Sc3+ — which is coloured in aqueous solution and why?

key_points: Ti3+ is coloured (violet) because it has one d-electron (3d1) that can undergo d-d transition; Sc3+ is colourless because it has no d-electrons (3d0) and d-d transitions are impossible

sub_questions.solution: Ti3+ is coloured in aqueous solution (violet colour) because it has the configuration [Ar] 3d1 — one unpaired d-electron is present. When visible light falls on Ti3+, the single d-electron undergoes a d-d transition (absorbing certain wavelengths of visible light), and the transmitted or reflected light appears coloured. Sc3+ has the configuration [Ar] 3d0 — no d-electrons are present and no d-d transitions are possible. Therefore Sc3+ is colourless in aqueous solution.

sub_questions.text: Cr अथवा Zn — उच्चतर तृतीय आयनन एन्थैल्पी कौन-सा और क्यों?
sub_questions.text_english: Cr or Zn — which has higher third ionisation enthalpy and why?

key_points: Zn has higher third ionisation enthalpy because removal of the 3rd electron from Zn (after losing 4s2 to give Zn2+) requires breaking the stable 3d10 configuration; Cr2+ still has d-electrons to lose more easily

sub_questions.solution: Zinc (Zn) has a higher third ionisation enthalpy than chromium (Cr). Zn has the configuration [Ar] 3d10 4s2. After losing two electrons (4s2), Zn2+ has the stable, completely filled 3d10 configuration. The removal of a third electron requires breaking into this stable 3d10 configuration, which requires very high energy. Cr has configuration [Ar] 3d5 4s1; after Cr2+ (3d4), the third ionisation removes a 3d electron which is less stabilised than the 3d10 configuration of Zn. Therefore Zn has a significantly higher third ionisation enthalpy.

sub_questions.text: अम्लीय माध्यम में MnO4− की Fe2+ आयन के साथ ऑक्सीकारक क्रिया के लिए आयनिक समीकरण।
sub_questions.text_english: Ionic equation for oxidizing action of MnO4− with Fe2+ ion in acidic medium.
sub_questions.solution: In acidic medium, permanganate (MnO4−) is reduced from Mn(+7) to Mn(+2), while Fe2+ is oxidised to Fe3+. Balancing: each MnO4− gains 5 electrons, each Fe2+ loses 1 electron, so 5 Fe2+ are needed per MnO4−. The ionic equation is: MnO4−(aq) + 8H+(aq) + 5Fe2+(aq) → Mn2+(aq) + 5Fe3+(aq) + 4H2O(l).

sub_questions.text: अम्लीय माध्यम में MnO4− की I− आयन के साथ ऑक्सीकारक क्रिया के लिए आयनिक समीकरण।
sub_questions.text_english: Ionic equation for oxidizing action of MnO4− with I− ion in acidic medium.
sub_questions.solution: In acidic medium, MnO4− oxidises I− to I2. Mn goes from +7 to +2 (gain of 5e−); I− goes from −1 to 0 in I2 (loss of 1e− per I−, or 2e− per I2). To balance: 2 MnO4− gain 10e−; 10 I− are oxidised to 5 I2. The ionic equation is: 2MnO4−(aq) + 16H+(aq) + 10I−(aq) → 2Mn2+(aq) + 5I2(aq) + 8H2O(l).

sub_questions.text: काले-भूरे ठोस (A) से (B) और (C) की पहचान करिए और अभिक्रियाएँ लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Identify (A), (B) and (C) and write the reactions involved.

key_points: A = MnO2 (black-brown solid, manganese dioxide)
B = K2MnO4 (potassium manganate, dark green)
C = KMnO4 (potassium permanganate, dark purple)

sub_questions.solution: Compound (A) is MnO2 (manganese dioxide), a black-brown solid. When MnO2 is fused with KOH in the presence of air (oxygen), it is oxidised to give the dark green coloured compound (B), potassium manganate (K2MnO4): 2MnO2 + 4KOH + O2 → 2K2MnO4 + 2H2O. Compound (B) K2MnO4 (manganate, Mn in +6 state, dark green) on electrolytic oxidation in alkaline medium gives compound (C), potassium permanganate (KMnO4, Mn in +7 state, dark purple): 2K2MnO4 → 2KMnO4 + 2K+ + 2e− (at anode). Thus A = MnO2, B = K2MnO4, C = KMnO4.

sub_questions.text: हरे रंग के यौगिक (B) के अम्लीय विलयन को रखने पर क्या होता है?
sub_questions.text_english: What happens when an acidic solution of the green compound (B) is allowed to stand for some time?

key_points: Disproportionation: K2MnO4 in acidic medium disproportionates to give KMnO4 (purple) and MnO2 (brown ppt) — Mn(+6) → Mn(+7) + Mn(+4)
3K2MnO4 + 2H2O → 2KMnO4 + MnO2 + 4KOH (or in acidic: 3MnO42− + 4H+ → 2MnO4− + MnO2 + 2H2O)

sub_questions.solution: When an acidic solution of potassium manganate K2MnO4 (compound B, Mn in +6 oxidation state) is allowed to stand for some time, it undergoes disproportionation. In acidic solution, Mn(+6) is unstable and disproportionates into Mn(+7) (permanganate, purple) and Mn(+4) (MnO2, brown precipitate): 3K2MnO4 + 2H2O → 2KMnO4 + MnO2↓ + 4KOH, or in ionic form: 3MnO42−(aq) + 4H+(aq) → 2MnO4−(aq) + MnO2(s) + 2H2O(l). This type of reaction is called disproportionation (a redox reaction in which the same species is simultaneously oxidised and reduced).
